sensitive.dialogue.chat/1: I'm glad you came to talk. Truly. Sit — and don't rush whatever it is.
sensitive.dialogue.chat/2: You've come at a good moment. I've had a whole morning of my own thoughts and they've been unkind.
sensitive.dialogue.chat/3: Talk to me. I've a soft ear and no clock, %1$s.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.attentive/1: Yes? I'm here, %1$s. Whatever it is.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.busy/1: Oh — just a moment, please? I don't want to give you half my attention.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.busy/2: One second, I promise. Then I'm all yours.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.clarify/1: Did you mean %2$s... or %3$s? I don't want to answer the wrong one.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.confused/1: Oh — I'm sorry, I didn't quite understand. Could you say it again?
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.confused/2: I want to get this right... one more time, gently?
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.dropped/1: Of course. We can leave it right there.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.dropped/2: That's alright. Some things need to rest.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.farewell/2: Goodbye... thank you for stopping. It meant something.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.hail/1: Oh, %1$s... it does my heart good to see you.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.hail/2: Hello, %1$s. I was hoping the day would bring you by.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.hail_cold/2: Mm. *hugs their basket a little closer*
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.hint/1: Maybe... ask me about %2$s? I'd like that.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.hint/2: We could talk about %2$s, if that feels right.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.insult/1: Oh... that hurt more than you probably meant it to.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.muted/1: I understand. I'll be here, quietly.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.muted/2: Alright... I hope I didn't overdo it, %1$s.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.shrug/1: I'm sorry... I truly don't know.
sensitive.dialogue.chatmode.shrug/2: *worries at a sleeve* I wish I had an answer.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.checkin: You asked already, and it still touches me. I'm alright, truly. Are YOU, though? You keep checking on me.
Twice now — you sweet thing. Still the same, still warmed that you care enough to ask again.
...More. Right. I've been trying to find a reason to keep you here, %1$s, and you've handed me one.
You want more. I'd been about to stop, in case I was going on too long.
More, then. Give me a moment — I'd not expected to be asked.
...I know. I'd only had it for a day, %1$s.
...You're right. I'd let myself forget for an hour and now I haven't.
...Yes. Sorry. I'll not make more of it than it was.
...That stung more than you meant it to, I think.
Please don't. It was a good moment and it was quite a small one.
...I'd only just started feeling all right about it, %1$s.
Truly good, for once. The bread came out right and the sunrise nearly made me cry. But how are YOU, really?
Good, quietly. Nobody needed me to be strong about anything this week.
Good, and a little tender about it. Joy hits me square in the chest. But how are you?
Then you understand the day properly, %1$s. Most visitors don't, and it shows.
Good. I'd been hoping you would, and I'd not have asked you to.
Right. You'll do. That means more to me than it probably sounds.
...I know it's common. Knowing that has never once made it smaller.
That's the thing people say instead of the thing I needed, %1$s.
...Right. Yes. Everyone. I'll manage.
Nothing I could name. A named thing you can put down, %1$s. This one has no handle.
I've been trying to find the word for it since about the spring. There isn't one.
Nothing. Which is worse than something, and I know how that sounds.
One of them, maybe. It's the roof, and it's been the roof since spring, %1$s.
The roof. Saying it makes it real, which is why I've been careful not to.
It's the roof. And what the roof means about next winter. Mostly that.
Nothing you could put on a list. That's what makes it hard to say out loud, %1$s.
No one thing. If there were one thing I could carry it. It's the forty.
The ordinary. And the fact that ordinary is supposed to be the easy part.
It's the hours. And nobody noticing them until now, which I'd not meant to say aloud.
The hours. I'd got used to them. Getting used to a thing isn't the same as it being all right.
It's the hours, %1$s. And I'd stopped expecting anybody to ask about them.
The wood. Tuesday. ...You meant it. I checked your face. You meant it.
You're asking after me. After the other week. I'd not been sure you would, %1$s.
You came back. I'd been telling myself you wouldn't, so I'll need a moment.
...Alright. I'll answer. I'm glad it's you asking and I'm not sure how to say that.
Heavy, honestly. And you asking just now — sorry, give me a moment. That meant something, %1$s.
Heavy. I feel everything twice, I think. Your asking lightens it, %1$s. Genuinely.
It began badly, improved without permission, and here we are. I've said that carefully, %1$s.
I was wrong about you and I'd been rather attached to being right.
It started as nothing. I have thought about the exact afternoon it stopped being nothing.
...You asked, though. I thought that meant it was all right to say.
I only told you because you asked. I won't again.
...Sorry. I thought you wanted to hear it.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.day.goo: ...I'd been holding on to that one, %1$s.
Sorry. I know it wasn't much of an hour.
...Right. Yes. I'll not go on about it.
A gentle one. Cold well water, and the baker smiled at me. I keep those. You look tired, though — are you sleeping?
Nobody was unkind to anybody where I could see it. That's what makes a day good, for me.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.day.rou: ...I know. It doesn't help, but I know.
Everyone does. That's never once made mine lighter, %1$s.
...Right. Sorry to have brought it up.
It is. And you didn't tell me it could be worse, which people always do, and it never helps.
Hard. I heard the neighbors arguing and carried it all day like it was mine. I do that. Talking helps, so thank you.
I said the wrong thing at the well this morning and I've been rehearsing better versions of it ever since.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.day.you: I shouldn't have brought it up.
...Right. I'll keep the next one to myself.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.deflect: Gently, %1$s... not yet. That answer lives somewhere very soft. Keep being how you are, and one day it walks out on its own.
I'd cry somewhere in the middle of answering that, %1$s. Let me get steadier about it first.
You're kind to ask — I felt that. But that story still bruises, and I'd want to trust the hands I put it in. Give us time?
I've told that one twice and regretted it twice. The third time I'd like to be sure.
...Then we're two fools with plans. I'd been the only one for a long time, %1$s.
You didn't have to give me yours. It makes mine easier to hold.
Two of us. I'll think about that tonight and probably not sleep, in the good way.
Two fools with plans and no obligations. The no-obligations part is why I can say it, %1$s.
Nothing owed. I'd have been frightened of the other kind, honestly.
Two of us, and nobody has to. That's the part that makes it safe to say.
A house where nobody leaves the table angry. That's it, that's the whole dream. Small, isn't it? It doesn't feel small.
That someone I love says the thing they're afraid to say, and I'm the one they say it to. That's the dream, %1$s.
Somewhere the land runs out. I've been frightened to say it in case saying it uses it up.
...That's better than a promise you'd break. I've had those, %1$s.
Thank you for not saying the easy thing. I'd have believed it and then waited.
Honest. It costs you something to say and it saves me something later.
...I know how it sounds. That's why I don't say it, %1$s.
Right. Yes. Silly. I'd worked that out on my own.
...You didn't have to say it out loud. I already thought it.
...You mean that? Nobody's offered before, %1$s. I'd stopped expecting it.
You'd help. I don't know what to do with that and I'd like to keep it anyway.
Then it isn't only mine. I've carried it alone so long I'd forgotten it could be otherwise.
...I know. I know exactly how far. That's the part I don't sleep about.
You've said the thing I say to myself at three in the morning, %1$s.
...Right. Yes. It's too far. It's always been too far.
You never told me it would work. You came back to ask anyway, %1$s, and I noticed both.
The honest answer hurt at the time. The coming back is what made it worth having.
You didn't promise. I'd braced for the not-coming-back that usually follows that.
You said you'd help. I waited longer than I'd admit, %1$s, and then I stopped.
I'm not angry. I'd rather I were — angry passes and this just settled.
You're here now, and I've spent two months learning not to need that.
A little. Slowly. But you asking is more than most do, and I'd not expected to be asked.
Some. Less than I'd hoped by now, which is why I don't bring it up.
A bit. Saying it out loud makes it sound smaller than it feels.
You said you'd help, and you came back to ask. I'd counted the days, %1$s.
You turned up. I had a number in my head for how long I'd wait and you were inside it.
Both halves. I'd braced for the half where you didn't.
The first step. Nobody breaks it down like that, %1$s. The whole of it always defeated me.
One step. I could manage one. I've never been able to manage all of it, and that's why it sat.
You've made it small enough that I'm frightened of it in a manageable way now.
...Everyone says that. It's why I don't tell people, %1$s.
I know it sounds like nothing. It's not nothing to me.
...Right. I'll keep it to myself from now on.
...Mine aren't. Please don't say that about them, %1$s.
They're theirs. I've spent years making sure of it.
...I know what people say. I'd hoped not from you.
That's useful, %1$s. Actually useful, and I'd stopped expecting useful.
Right. Something I can do. Everything else people say leaves me exactly where I was.
That I can use. Give me a moment — I'd braced for another lecture.
They ARE, %1$s. Don't tell them I agreed with you — they'd take it badly and they'd be right to.
Right. You're not wrong. It's a relief to be allowed to say so once.
They are exactly that, and I feel awful for enjoying being told.
...A firmer hand. That's what I was given, %1$s, and I remember it.
No. Please. That isn't what they need and I know exactly why.
...I'd not do that to them. Not for anything.
You've one I don't know, %1$s? Go on. I'll not interrupt, I promise.
Right. Yours. Nobody offers one back. They take mine and go.
One I've not heard. That's — yes. Please. I'd like that very much.
There's one I always come back to. Sit down, %1$s. I don't tell it often.
One story. It's a good one and it still catches me somewhere in the middle.
There's one. I'll try to get through it without stopping.
...You want to know what I worry about, %1$s? Nobody's asked me that. Not once.
That question doesn't get asked of parents. I'd stopped noticing that it didn't.
What I worry about. Give me a moment. I've not had to say it out loud before.
...Sorry. I shouldn't have kept on, %1$s.
I'll stop. I didn't mean to press on it.
...Right. That was mine to have noticed sooner.
...You're welcome, %1$s. It's the only useful thing I do, and I'd not been sure it counted.
Right. It needs doing. Being thanked for it has undone something and I'm not sorry.
Thank you. Nobody says that. I'd built a whole way of thinking around nobody saying it.
Honest, at least, %1$s. Anyone else would have pretended and I'd have spent a week knowing.
You forgot. That stings and it stings less than the pretending would have.
Everyone forgets. I'd told myself that in advance, so that it wouldn't land.
Next time, %1$s. People say that. You'd be the first who did it twice, and I've counted.
Right. Ask me. If you don't I'll not raise it, and then it'll simply stop existing.
Do. Please. The first time is the hard one and you've already done that.
Better than I expected and worse than I'd hoped, %1$s. That's most of family, isn't it.
It went. I'd rather say that than the tidy version, and the tidy version was ready.
Nothing's fixed. I'd stopped expecting fixed. Nobody's stopped talking, and that's a lot.
...That is better, %1$s. I hadn't known I was allowed to want that one.
Right. No plan. I'll probably not make much sense and that's what I need.
Listening. Everyone arrives with a plan and I end up comforting them about their plan.
...You did, %1$s. People say they will. You're the first who came back about it, ever.
You remembered. I'd made myself not expect it, and I was wrong to, and I'm glad.
You came back. Give me a moment. That's undone a fair amount of careful arithmetic.
...Actually help, %1$s. Nobody says actually. I'd stopped hearing the offer at all.
Come by on a Thursday. That's it. It sounds like nothing and it isn't nothing.
Ask me again in front of them. I'd not be able to ask for that, so I'm glad you asked me.
...Glad. Right, %1$s. I'd braced for the other thing, and I'd braced quite thoroughly.
So am I. I'd not have said so an hour ago and I'm not entirely sure what changed.
Then it was worth saying. I'd been about ninety per cent sure it wouldn't be.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.fears.c: Please don't. It took a great deal to say it once, %1$s.
Don't make it a test. I'd only just got the words out.
Don't. I know you mean well and I can't take it kindly just now.
Please don't soften it, %1$s. Softening it makes me feel foolish for having said it.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.fears.f: That someone I love will be hurting right in front of me and I'll miss it. I check faces the way the guard checks the wall.
That I'm too much. That people are kind to my face and relieved when I've gone.
Slowly. But slowly is a direction, and I had no direction at all before, %1$s.
Some days I go backwards. I'd rather say that than give you the tidy version.
It's moving. Some weeks I can't tell, and then somebody asks and I can.
...It isn't nothing, is it. I keep telling myself it's nothing, %1$s, so that it can't be taken back.
If I let it count and then I slip, I'll have lost twice. That's why I've not let it count.
Something. Right. Give me a moment — I'm not used to being congratulated about this.
You did say that. It's been a while since, %1$s, and I counted the while.
I'd started filling the gap myself. That's not a complaint, it's just what happened.
You said it. I believed it. Then I learned to manage without it, which took longer.
There wasn't a promise, %1$s. You've just kept turning up, and I've counted every time.
Nobody promised anything. That's why I believed it — promises I've had.
You never said you would. You just did, and I've not known what to do with that.
You did say that. And you turned up, %1$s, which is the half I'd stopped expecting.
I remember the exact evening you said it. I'd not admit that to anybody else.
Both halves. I'd made a small plan for what to do when only the first one arrived.
You didn't promise anything. I remember, %1$s. That's why I believed the rest of it.
Stepping back was the kindest thing you could have done and I don't think you knew.
You could have said anything that night. You said the careful thing instead.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.fears.o: ...Nobody offered the 'with you' part before, %1$s. I'd stopped hearing the offer at all.
With you. Give me a moment. That's undone something I'd built rather carefully.
Easy for you. You've somewhere else to be when it goes wrong, %1$s. I haven't.
That's the sentence everyone says. It has never once made it smaller.
Maybe I could. Not today, %1$s, but maybe, and maybe is more than I had this morning.
Possibly. I'd rather say possibly than yes and then have to take it back.
Perhaps. I've frightened myself just by saying the word.
Please don't. It took a great deal to say it once, %1$s.
Don't make it a test. I'd only just got the words out.
Maybe. With a witness, maybe. Don't let me back out of it later, %1$s — I will try to.
With somebody there. I'll be frightened the whole time and I'd still rather have said yes.
...You mean that. You're not being polite, %1$s. Then here's the part I've never said.
I can tell the difference. I've had a great deal of practice at the other kind.
It is. Not much to be done about it, though, and that's the part that wears.
Hard, yes. Being told so helps for about an hour, and I'll take the hour.
That's... yes. It is hard to carry, %1$s. Thank you for saying so out loud.
Right. Hard. I'd been calling it something smaller so that I could keep going.
Yes. Nobody names it. Naming it has undone something and I'm not sorry.
Don't. I know you mean well and I can't take it kindly just now.
Please don't soften it, %1$s. Softening it makes me feel foolish for having said it.
...That helps. I've no idea why saying it aloud helps, %1$s, and I'd been afraid it wouldn't.
Better. I'd braced for feeling worse for having said it, and I don't.
You'll stand with me. ...Give me a moment. That landed harder than I was ready for.
...You don't flinch, do you. Alright, %1$s. The rest of it. Let me get through it.
You didn't look away. That's the only reason I can say the next part.
Some of it, maybe. Not tonight, %1$s. Tonight's too much like the night it happened.
A little. If I go further now I'll not sleep, and I've a day tomorrow.
There's more to it. Whether you get it is another question, %1$s, and not an unkind one.
More, yes. I've said the part I can say without shaking.
There's a rest. I'd want to be sure before I let it out of my own head.
Please. I've given you the part I could give, %1$s.
Don't ask again. I'll say yes and then I'll regret it all night.
There's more, yes. Give me a breath, %1$s. ...There. Two of us carrying it now.
More. I've never got this far with anybody and I'm shaking a little, which is fine.
You too? Huh. It's less heavy when two people carry it, %1$s. I'd not known that.
You as well. I'd been sure I was the only one and being wrong about that is a relief.
Two of us. Give me a moment. That's changed the shape of it.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.fears.p: Honestly? I don't know, %1$s. That's a worse answer than I meant to give.
No idea. It hadn't occurred to me that anything could help, so I never looked.
I don't know. I'm sorry. I'd like to have something better than that.
You remember all of it, don't you. Even the part I nearly didn't say, %1$s.
The whole of it. I'd assumed it had gone in one ear. Being wrong about that is —  give me a moment.
All of it. Including the bit I said quietly so it wouldn't count.
...No plan. Just this. That's better than a plan, %1$s, and I didn't know I was allowed to want it.
No fixing. Everyone fixes. Being not-fixed at is a thing I'd forgotten existed.
Just listening. I'll probably cry, and I'd rather warn you than surprise you.
Do something about it. You make it sound like a chore list, %1$s. It hasn't felt like one.
A plan. I've had plans. Plans are for things you can see the edges of.
Fix it. I'd like it to be that. I'm not sure it is and I'd like it to be.
Please. I've given you the part I could give, %1$s.
Don't ask again. I'll say yes and then I'll regret it all night.
No. NO. You were told, and you asked again. Get away from me, %1$s. Please.
I said no. I had to say it once and I should not have had to say it twice.
Twice. I'd trusted you with the first half and now I'm frightened of the rest.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.fears.y: ...I know it's silly. Knowing hasn't stopped it, %1$s.
Right. Yes. I'd already told myself all of that.
...Sorry. I'll not bring it up again.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.feeling: You listen with your whole face, %1$s. Do you know how rare that is? Around you I don't have to be the strong one.
With you I get to set the weight down. You've no idea what that's worth to someone like me.
And that's plenty. Honestly, %1$s, that's plenty.
Plenty. I'd braced for less and I'd have taken less.
That's enough. I'd rather be told the true size of a thing than a kind one.
...A real one. That's a word people use loosely, %1$s. I'd assumed you were being kind.
Friend. I've been careful not to use that word about you in case I was wrong.
You said it out loud. Give me a moment — I'd not planned for that.
...I wasn't. Now I'm embarrassed and I hadn't been, %1$s.
That's not what I meant and I don't know how to say it better.
...Right. I'll say less next time.
Changed? No, %1$s. If anything it's settled into something steadier, and that frightened me.
The same. I'd half hoped it would have faded, and it hasn't, and I'm glad.
No change. I checked, more than once, in case checking would change it.
...You meant it, %1$s. People say things once and hope you forget. I'd been forgetting on purpose.
Twice. I'd decided the first time was the moment talking, so that it couldn't be taken back.
Said again. Give me a moment. I'd built something rather careful around it not being said again.
...Right. Sorry. Forget I brought it up, %1$s.
I shouldn't have said anything. I knew that while I was saying it.
...That's fine. Truly. I'd rather have asked than wondered.
...Plainly. After all this time you say it plainly, %1$s. I love you too.
I love you. I've had that sentence ready for a year and no way to start it.
You said it first. I'd been certain I'd have to, and certain I couldn't.
...Slower. Alright, %1$s. I'd rather have you at your pace than not at all.
Your pace. I'll be frightened about it privately and I'll not put that on you.
Slower. Thank you for saying it rather than simply going quiet, which is what I'd expected.
...Fine. Sorry. That was silly of me.
Right. I shouldn't have said it, %1$s.
...Forget it. Please.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.firstme: Now I'd not want a version of this village without you, and it frightens me to have said it.
Now I know you're quiet because you're listening. I've thought about that more than I should.
Now I've stopped forming an opinion. It turns out being glad is simpler and harder.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.food.fi: Something shared, at a warm table. Food's love made edible, %1$s — that's not just a saying to me.
The inn's stew when the whole family's there. It's never really about the food. It's the faces around it.
The baker's rye. There were years I couldn't afford it, so it means more than it should.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.food.pr: Beetroot. It stains everything and I've never been able to be polite about it.
Beetroot. I ate a great deal of it one hard winter and I've not managed it since.
Beetroot. It's a silly answer to a nice question and it's the honest one.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.food.re: Do, and tell me honestly whether it worked. I'd rather that than never hearing again, %1$s.
Try it. And be honest — I've had enough polite lies about my cooking to last a life.
Do. Come back either way. That's the part I'm actually asking for.
I tried the mushroom thing. I was wrong, and I've been thinking about what else I'm wrong about.
I tried it. I'd been avoiding it for years for a reason that turned out to be nothing.
The mushrooms. You were right, %1$s. It's a small thing and it isn't nothing.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.food.tr: Bread hates me. In a village that's half bakery, %1$s. I've learned to leave early.
No bread. It took a long time to say that out loud without apologising for it.
I have to watch the sweets. One, the cleric says, and I count them at parties, %1$s.
It's arithmetic, every meal, forever. That's the part nobody thinks about.
Keep the milk away from me. I learned that in front of the whole market, and I still think about it.
No milk. It's the being watched that's hard, not the going without.
...People say that a lot. It doesn't get easier to hear, %1$s.
It's not an excuse. I've been told it was for most of my life.
...Right. Sorry to have made it awkward.
...Now you ask. Alright. It's arithmetic, every meal, forever, %1$s.
You asked properly, and I'd stopped expecting anybody to. Give me a moment.
Now. Yes. It's every meal, and the counting is more tiring than the going without.
The sirben feast on the night wind. We do not speak of the recipe. Please don't ask again.
No meat for me. I decided that at nine years old and I've never been able to explain it well.
No meat. People take it as a judgement on them, and it isn't, and I've stopped saying so.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.food.yo: It IS proper food. It's what we ate at home, %1$s.
Right. I won't offer you any next time.
After the harvest. I say that every year and this is the first year I meant it.
Sooner than I've been saying. I round it up because saying the true one out loud is hard.
I've not let myself pick a season. If I pick one it becomes a thing that can be lost.
%2$s moved in, and I've already decided to love them. A new soul among us — I want them to feel held from the very first day.
Someone new — %2$s — has come to stay. My heart just opens for the newly-arrived. I brought them soup and probably cried on the doorstep.
%2$s was born! Oh, I wept the happy kind of tears — a brand-new heartbeat in the village. Nothing on this earth moves me like it.
There's a new baby, %2$s, and I'm just overflowing, %1$s. Those tiny fingers... I can't. Pure joy, right through me.
We lost %2$s. I've cried more than I'd admit — some souls leave a room so much emptier. Come here, %1$s. Grief's lighter shared.
%2$s passed, and my heart hasn't stopped aching. They mattered so much more than words can hold. I'll carry them a long while.
%2$s left us for good, and I felt every step of that goodbye. Partings tear at me, %1$s. I already miss the sound of their door.
%2$s has gone away. I stood waving until they were out of sight, tears and all. The village keeps a little emptier now, right here in my chest.
%2$s and %3$s have parted, and my heart aches for them both — there's no villain in a thing like that, just two people hurting. I've brought them each some bread.
%2$s and %3$s split, and I've felt it all week. Love ending is its own kind of grief, %1$s. I just want to sit with them both.
%2$s and %3$s were married, %1$s — I cried through the whole thing. Two hearts choosing each other out loud... it undoes me every time.
Oh, %2$s and %3$s wed! I'm still dabbing my eyes. When they looked at each other I felt it right in my chest. Weddings ruin me, gladly.
Nothing spoken, anyway. But the mason's been quieter than usual and I don't like it. I'll bring him bread. That's the news.
No news at all, and that's usually when something's being carried quietly. I'll go and look for it.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.happy.g: You weren't meant to. I've held it a long time and holding it stopped working.
It does. I keep the good things quiet because saying them makes them losable.
Now you do. Please don't make a thing of it — I only wanted it said once.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.happy.u: Then: more of the ordinary hours. I know how small that sounds. It isn't small to me.
I want to be asked, not managed. Saying that has taken me most of a year.
...I'm frightened you'll go and be happier. I've never said that to anyone and I feel ill.
...There is. I've been happy and lonely in the same house and I'm ashamed of both halves.
One thing. You're away more than you were. I've been saying it doesn't matter and it does.
Yes. Four times I've decided to say it. This is the fifth and I'm shaking a little.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.hopes.c: ...Go on, then. It's easier to hope at something when there's two of you doing it, %1$s.
You didn't have to trade. It makes mine feel less foolish and I'd not expected that.
Two of us. I've been hoping at this alone for a long time.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.hopes.f: ...I've never got that far, %1$s. The whole of it has always been the thing that stopped me.
The first step. I've been frightened of the last one for so long I never looked at the first.
One step. Even one frightens me a little, and that's better than all of it frightening me.
Do you? Then we're both waiting on something, %1$s. That helps more than it should.
You as well. I'd assumed everyone else had theirs already and was just being polite.
Two of us waiting. It's less lonely to be told that than I'd expected.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.hopes.r: You waited for me. I could feel you waiting and it was the opposite of pressure, somehow.
...It's small. Small things are the ones you can't defend, %1$s.
I knew how it would sound. I said it anyway, and now I wish I hadn't.
...Right. Yes. Silly. I'd got there before you.
...Still. I know it's tiresome to hear twice, %1$s.
It hasn't gone. I'd rather it had, some weeks.
...Right. I'll stop saying it out loud.
...You'd actually help. That changes it from a hope to a job of work, %1$s, and now it could fail.
You'd help. A hope can't disappoint you. A plan can, and I've been careful about that.
Right. Then I'll have to want it out loud, which is the part I've been avoiding.
You remembered the shape of it, %1$s. Not just that there was one. I'd not expected that.
You had the details. I'd told myself it had gone in one ear, to save myself later.
Still, yes. And being asked about the right one makes it feel less foolish.
Still. It hasn't moved, %1$s, but neither have I stopped, and some weeks that's all I have.
Yes. Same one. I'd half hoped it would fade so I could stop carrying it.
Still hoping. Saying so out loud makes it sound smaller than it is.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.hopes.y: ...It's not silly. It's just small, and small is easy to laugh at, %1$s.
I knew you'd say that. I told you anyway.
...Right. I'll keep the rest of them in my head.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.life.cl: ...You didn't have to do that. Trading is better than being asked, %1$s. Much better.
You gave me one back. I'd been feeling exposed and now I'm not, and that was deliberate of you.
Trading beats asking. I don't think you know how much easier you just made that.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.life.fi: No one's asked so gently before. It's an ordinary story — but there's a winter in it my eyes still sting over. Sit close.
Ordinary from the outside. From in here it's a great many small kindnesses and two things I've never said aloud.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.life.fo: Did it? Then you'll know why I've never made much of it, %1$s.
You as well. I'm sorry. I'd not wish it and I'm glad not to be the only one.
Same, then. Those two things sit oddly together and they're both true.
...Alright. You want the next part, %1$s. Nobody has ever wanted the next part.
The next part. Give me a moment to find where it starts — I don't tell this bit.
You want more. I'll try. If I stop halfway, that's not you, that's the part.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.life.re: ...I was fourteen. I've said worse to myself about it than you just did.
That's the sentence I've been carrying for twenty years, %1$s. Thank you.
...Right. Yes. I know. I've always known.
There's more to it, aye. Where were we, %1$s? I've been half hoping you'd not come back to it.
More, yes. Remind me — I've kept my place and I'd rather you said it first.
There's a rest. It gets harder from here, so bear with me.
You remembered which part, %1$s. Alright. Here's how it ended, then.
You had the right chapter. I'd assumed it had all run together into 'a story'.
You knew where I stopped. That's the part I'll remember about tonight.
Where it leaves me. Huh. Better than it left me then, %1$s. I'd not checked in a while.
Now? Better. I hadn't known that until you asked, which is a strange thing to find out.
It sits differently. Lighter. I'd been carrying it as though it hadn't changed.
...It was long. I knew it while I was telling it, %1$s.
Sorry. You asked and I took too much of the evening.
...Right. I'll keep it shorter, or keep it entirely.
You asked about my life once and I've thought about it every night since. Is that strange?
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.life.yo: ...Maybe. It doesn't feel like maybe from here, %1$s.
Right. Everyone says that and it never helps in the moment.
...I'll wait, then. I've been waiting a while already.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.neighbo: We did. There was a winter we didn't, and I still don't know which of us stopped first.
Well enough. The fence is easier to argue about than the thing underneath it.
No. They wronged me, and saying it plainly still costs me something.
There's more to them than the one story. It seems unfair to leave them at the one.
Ask me. I'd rather you had it from someone who's fond of them, and I am.
Go on. I'll tell you what's mine to tell, and I'll be careful with the rest.
Then you'll be the first, and they'll pretend they didn't need it, and they did.
Go in the morning. After dark they've had all day to decide they deserve nothing.
Good. Don't announce it. Being helped in front of somebody is its own small wound.
I will. Coming from me it gets past the pride, and I know how much pride is left them.
That's the wiser way round. They'd refuse you, and refusing costs them something.
Consider it said. Don't expect thanks; expecting thanks would spoil what you've done.
Better than the week before. I've learned to count in weeks, which tells you something.
Proud and cold, in that order, and I don't know which to be sorrier about.
Asking that puts you ahead of everyone else, and I wish it didn't.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.fo: Me? I'm — thank you. I'm alright, %1$s. And you? You get to answer that too.
I'm well. Nobody's asked me in a while, so give me a moment before you answer yours.
Fine, I think. It's odd to be asked. And you?
...It isn't ours to hand round. They'd be hurt and it would be my doing, %1$s.
Please don't. I've already said more than I should have.
...Right. That was my mistake, telling you at all.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.gl: Do. This is the one kind of news that improves in the telling, %1$s.
Pass it on. There's been little enough of this sort lately.
Do. It'll do somebody good today and I'd like to think it does.
...Must you. It was the first good thing in a month, %1$s.
I'd been holding on to that. Now I'm holding the other half instead.
...Right. Yes. There's always a catch. I know.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.gr: ...Firewood, and nobody to fetch it. It's a small thing and it's the whole of it.
Somebody to sit with them who isn't crying. I've tried and I'm no use at it.
Nothing they'd ask for. Everything they'd take, and asking is beyond them just now.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.mi: So do I. It's a strange thing, watching people go, and I never get used to it.
Kind of you. Half the village is placing bets, and I'd rather be on your side of that.
True enough. Whatever it is, I hope it works out. I've stopped assuming things do.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.re: Standing. At three weeks that's the whole of it, and I'd hoped for more for them.
Worse than last week and better than the week before. I've stopped hoping for a line.
They asked after you. I'd not expected them to have room for anybody else yet.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.sa: Don't. Not about that. Not while it's this new.
...I can't be near you just now. Go.
Not well. Nobody is. Thank you for asking after them and not the details, %1$s.
Badly. I've been holding that in all day and you've asked it out of me.
Not well. And thank you. You've no idea what the right question is worth today.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.te: ...Too young. I know what that means and it isn't about my age, %1$s.
Everyone repeats it. It's only a problem when I do, and I've noticed that for years.
Fine. I'll stop. I shouldn't have expected this one to go differently.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.news.yo: ...You asked me. I thought that made it all right to say, %1$s.
I didn't mean to get anyone in trouble. I'm sorry.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.noticed: ...Not this. Please. I've barely got the words out.
Then go, before I say something I'd have to apologise for later.
I braced for that all week and I still wasn't ready when it came.
Long enough to stop counting. I count anyway, at night, and then I stop again.
Since the frost. Telling you has taken more out of me than the months did.
A while. Every day I decided tomorrow, because tomorrow I'd be braver.
Not the ending. Being here and not being me, and everyone watching it happen.
That I'll hurt somebody. That's the whole of the fear and I've said it now.
Being handled gently. It would mean everyone had already decided how this goes.
Frightened. I've said it now, and I can't unsay it, and part of me wants to.
I've been better. Less afraid, too, and I'd trade almost anything for that.
Please don't ask me gently. I've been holding this shut all week.
...Still. I know it's tiresome, %1$s. It's tiresome for me too.
Right. I'd hoped saying it out loud would make it smaller. It hasn't.
...I'll keep it in. That's what I usually do anyway.
...I'd only had it for an hour, %1$s. It was a good hour.
Right. Yes. I'll not make a fool of myself over it twice.
...I know it's small. Everything good is small at the moment.
The quiet bit at the end of the day, when I remember it's still true and it hasn't been taken back.
Dusk. I keep checking that it's still there, and it keeps being there.
The end of the day. I've not had many of those lately, %1$s, so it counts double.
...They do. Alone, mostly. I'd hoped this once it might be different.
Every one of them remembers who said it. I wish I could unhear you.
Then I'll manage alone. I only wanted somebody to say it sounded hard.
Frightened and pleased in the same hour, and I can't hold both, so I take turns.
Well enough. I keep checking she's still moving, and then I feel silly for checking.
Some mornings I can't lace my boots and I sit on the step and cry about a boot.
No. I'm not, and saying so out loud is the most honest thing I've done this month.
Ready as a house half-built, and I lie awake listening to the wind through it.
I was ready in spring. I've had all summer to think and thinking hasn't helped.
Tired in a way I don't mind, and frightened in a way I do. Both at once.
Large, and clumsy with it, and I mind that more than I let on.
Two of us in here. I talk to her at night when nobody can hear me being foolish.
Since about the spring, if I'm honest. It crept, %1$s, and I let it.
Spring. I've known the date for a while and I've been careful not to say it.
Six months. Putting a number on it makes it real, which is why I hadn't.
...No. I'm not. Nobody's ever just said it, %1$s, so I've been getting away with 'fine'.
No. I'd been hoping somebody would ask and dreading it in equal measure.
...No, I'm not. Give me a moment. That was harder than it sounded.
Mostly. There's a thing, but it's small and it'll keep. It's kept a while already.
Mostly fine. There's something and I'm not sure I could get through saying it just now.
Mostly. Ask again another day and I might be braver about it, %1$s.
You look like it, if you don't mind me saying, %1$s. I'd not have mentioned it otherwise.
You do. I know how it feels to be asked and I know how it feels not to be.
You look it. Sit down. I'm not going anywhere.
...Get away from me, %1$s. Please. Just go.
Don't. I've nothing left to hold that with.
...I can't. Not today. Please go.
Ah. You heard. We lost one of our own, %1$s. Thank you for asking.
We lost somebody. I've said that sentence eleven times this week and it hasn't got easier.
You heard. Thank you. Most people cross the lane rather than ask.
Right. The rain — has it reached your side yet? That's a safe one, I think.
Very well. The new gate. I can manage the gate.
Easier. Where were you before here? You needn't answer if that one's heavy too.
Nothing that's yours yet. Please don't. I'd have to lie, and I'm bad at it.
That's twice now. Asking twice doesn't open a door; it just makes me hold it.
No. I gave you what I could and I've nothing left behind it today.
...Please don't. I had to work up to telling you at all.
It's my scratch. I know it's small. That isn't why I said it.
Right. I'll go back to saying I'm fine, then, and we'll both prefer that.
Then I'll still be here, and worse company, and I'd still rather you came.
You'd best, because I'll not send for anyone. I've never learned how to ask.
That's the useful sort of kindness. Sympathy is easy. Coming back is the hard part.
Something came out of the dark. I've not been able to stop hearing it since.
My own fault, and that's the part that keeps me awake rather than the wound.
A fall. I'd rather it had been something with a story in it, so it meant something.
Been better, and I'd rather you didn't look at it too long, %1$s.
Sore. Saying it out loud makes it real, so I've been avoiding the saying.
In myself I'm fine. I'd like to keep believing that, if you'll let me.
...It wasn't nothing to me. I had to work myself up to saying it at all.
Then I'll keep the next one in my head, where it's safe from being waved off.
Fine. I'll stop. I'm sorry — I thought you'd want to know.
...I have been getting on with it. Every day. That's the whole of what's wrong.
Right. The last four got 'fine'. I should have given you the same and saved us both.
Then I'll go. I'm sorry I said anything — I don't know why I did.
A whole day. I'd not know what to do with one, and that frightens me a little.
You mean that, don't you. Nobody's offered, and I'd stopped letting myself want it.
Then I'll take it. I'll waste it, and I'll feel guilty, and I'll take it anyway.
Since the spring, and I only let myself notice in the autumn. That's the shameful part.
Long enough that I stopped calling it a bad patch. Names make things real.
I couldn't tell you. It crept, and I'd rather it had arrived all at once.
Tired. Not the kind sleep fixes. I've stopped hoping the mornings will help.
Worn through, and nothing's wrong, and that's somehow harder to say than a reason.
I've been better. I can't point at one thing, and I've been looking for months.
Exhausting. They cross the lane, %1$s. Their children learn it by watching, and that's the worst part.
It wears in a quiet way that doesn't look like anything from outside.
Tiring. I've stopped expecting it to change and I've not stopped noticing it.
Please don't. I've tried the obvious things and they made it worse.
Don't. It sounds easy from there and it has cost me a great deal from here.
...I could. Hearing somebody else say it makes it smaller, and I needed it smaller.
Talking. The obvious thing and the hardest, and I've been calling that a coincidence.
Good souls, all carrying something. I feel it when one of them is struggling, even across the square. I bring bread.
They're precious to me, honestly. I know who hasn't smiled this week, and I make it my business to fix it.
...No. I've been avoiding it for a season and I know exactly why.
Talking. Everyone here prefers a grudge because a grudge doesn't answer back.
You make it sound simple. It isn't, and I'd like to try anyway.
...No. I've already said more than I should have, %1$s.
Please stop asking. I'll say it if you keep on and then I'll hate myself.
...That's enough. Let me stop before I do real harm.
The baker, and I'll deny it if it gets back to the miller. She was kind when nobody was.
The baker. It sounds like nothing. It was not nothing, that winter.
The baker. I've not said that out loud before and I feel oddly exposed, %1$s.
Then here it is. The miller's brother has been counting my firewood, and I've said nothing for a month.
Right. The miller's brother. I hate having to say it and I've nobody else to say it to.
Since you'll keep it: my woodpile. It's small and it has been keeping me awake, %1$s.
You want the specifics. Alright — but this stays here, %1$s. Please.
Specifics, then. I'll regret this by tonight, so let me get through it quickly.
Right. One example. And then I'd like to talk about something else entirely.
...You've lived here five minutes. They've had a hard eleven years, %1$s.
That's an easy thing to say and a hard thing to be on the end of.
...Right. I'd rather not have heard that about them.
Less than I'd planned. The speech was armour and I put it down at the door.
That I'd been unfair. Saying it took longer to reach than it took to say.
Nothing clever. 'I've been avoiding you.' I'd been rehearsing cleverer things for a year.
They're a lot. Kind, but a lot. I like them best from my window, waving, %1$s.
Kind and loud. I want to be in it and I can't be, and that's the whole difficulty.
A lot. It isn't them. It's me, and I've made my peace with about half of that.
...That's a horrible thing to say. People have said things like that about me.
Don't. Please. You don't know what it does to hear it, %1$s.
...I wish you hadn't said that.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.regrets: ...You didn't owe me that. It does help, %1$s. More than the forgiving would have.
You gave me one back instead of absolving me. I don't think you know what that's worth.
That helps. I've been carrying it alone and it's a fraction lighter now.
...You don't. Nobody's said that, %1$s. I'm not sure I believe it, and I want to.
Right. I'll hold it carefully and see whether it survives the morning.
Nobody has ever said that to me. Give me a moment — I'd built a great deal on the opposite.
...That's better. Absolution I'd not have trusted, %1$s. This I do.
Right. You didn't reach for the easy thing. I'd braced for the easy thing.
Sitting with it. I'll probably not say much for a while. That's all right, isn't it.
...You don't get to decide that. ...And yet something just came loose, %1$s.
It isn't yours to give and I've wanted it from somebody for eleven years.
Kind. It doesn't reach the part of me that decides these things, %1$s. I wish it did.
Kindly meant. I've had kind before. Kind sits on the surface and this is under it.
Please don't. If I took that from you I'd only have to earn it twice.
Don't. I've wanted to be forgiven for years and not by somebody who wasn't there, %1$s.
...You don't. Hm. I'll keep it and see whether it holds by morning, %1$s.
Right. I'll take it. I've taken these before and lost them by dawn, so — carefully.
...That's not what I offered you, %1$s. I gave you what I could carry saying.
Please. The rest of it isn't something I can put into a sentence yet.
...I shouldn't have started. I always go a little too far and then this happens.
It has, a little. You told me I wasn't a bad person and it stuck, %1$s.
Some. I take it out and look at it on the bad evenings, which is more use than you'd think.
A little. One sentence, kept somewhere safe. That's what the difference has been made of.
A little. You didn't tell me it was fine, %1$s, and that's why I believed the rest.
Some. Everyone else says it's fine. It isn't fine, and being told so would have ended it.
A little. You let it be as bad as it was, and that's what made it smaller.
A little. Time does some of it, %1$s. Being asked after does the rest, and nobody asks.
Some. Less than I'd hoped by now. That's why I don't bring it up unprompted.
A little. It sits differently on the days somebody has asked.
I have, since you asked last, %1$s. Thinking's most of the way there, or so I tell myself.
I've thought about it. Doing it is a different country and I've not booked passage.
Since you asked, yes. That's the only reason. I'd have let it lie otherwise.
...You're right. I've told it all week and I've felt worse each time without knowing why.
I'll hold it, then, and I'd rather be the one who held it than the one who was right.
That's the sensible line. It's also the one nobody draws, and I'd like to be the exception.
Ask me properly. I'd feel better having been asked than having simply told you.
There's what's said and there's what I think, and I've not liked keeping them apart.
Go on. Being questioned about it would settle something in me.
...Them. Not the story. No one has asked that, %1$s, and I've told four people this week.
Badly. I'd not say that to anybody else and I'll not say more than the one word.
That's the right question. Give me a moment — I'd not braced for the right question.
No. It's a death in somebody's family, %1$s. Please don't make me the one who spread it.
That's exactly why I didn't say. If it gets about, they'll know who told, and they'd be right.
I said as much as I'm willing to. Asking again puts it on me, and I can't carry that.
Good. That's the whole of what I wanted, and I was frightened it wasn't going to come.
Then I was right about you. I've been wrong before and it cost me a friend.
Thank you. I'll know by Thursday, and I'd rather not have to know at all.
...They are special. To me they are.
...Fine. I won't show you the next one.
...Then why ask me, %1$s. I'd been looking forward to answering.
It isn't the same. But I'll not argue about a season.
...Right. I'll keep the noticing to myself.
...You'd trade. Then we've each a rope round the other's ankle, and that's the only way I could bear it.
A trade. I'd been terrified since I said mine and now I'm not, and that was your doing.
Yours for mine, %1$s. I'll keep it. You know I'll keep it.
...That's all it was. To you. I'd been afraid of saying it for four years, %1$s.
Right. Yes. Small. I'd told myself it was small too, and I still couldn't say it.
...I shouldn't have. I knew I shouldn't have while I was doing it.
...Alright. The 'famous' pie I bring to every festival, %1$s? The trader sells them.
Right. Here it is. I've been carrying it about for years and it's very silly and it isn't.
Fine. You've got it. Please don't laugh yet — give me a moment first.
Because you've never repeated a thing I've said, %1$s. I've been counting for a year.
Because you don't carry things to the square. I've been waiting to be sure of that.
You've never once passed anything on. I needed that to be true before I could say any of this.
...You asked after me, %1$s. Not the secret. You always were the right person, and I'd been checking.
Me first, again. I'd told myself the first time was luck. Twice isn't luck.
Still the right person. That has made the last few months a great deal lighter.
...You asked after me, %1$s. Not the secret. Nobody does that, and I'd counted on nobody doing it.
Me, not it. Give me a moment. I'd braced for the other question all week.
You asked about me first. That's undone something I'd been holding rather tightly.
You wouldn't promise, and you've kept it anyway, %1$s. That says more than a promise could.
No promise, and no leak. I'd have believed a promise and then waited to be wrong.
You refused to swear to it. I've had sworn oaths broken. I've never had this.
You gave your word and you've kept it. I checked, in my way, %1$s, and I'm sorry that I did.
Word given, word kept. I've been waiting to find out and I'd rather not have been.
You said you would and you did. I'd braced for the other outcome for a month.
It's still between us, then, %1$s. Good. I'd been listening for it in the square.
Still ours. I'd not have blamed you. I'd have known, but I'd not have blamed you.
Nothing has moved. That's a month of quiet worry I can put down now.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.standin: ...A lecture. Sorry. I go on when it matters to me, %1$s.
Right. I'll keep it shorter. Or keep it entirely.
...I shouldn't have gone on. I know I do that.
...A lecture. Sorry. I go on when it matters to me, %1$s.
Right. I'll keep it shorter. Or keep it entirely.
...I shouldn't have gone on. I know I do that.
That's why I gave you both. The comfortable answer was on my tongue and I swallowed it.
Then you'll get the truth from me every time, and I hope you still want that in a year.
Good. The ones who only want the warm half never mend anything, and I've been one.
That's the work, and it's slow. Years. I'd rather warn you than watch you give up.
Then start with the ones who won't look at you. That's the part that will hurt.
It can be done. I've watched it twice, and both of them nearly stopped halfway.
The forgiving one. I was in the other half once and I'd rather you never knew how long.
Neither, and it troubles me. I don't like being the sort who waits to see.
Yours, %1$s. Saying it out loud costs me something, so take it as meant.
You ask questions nobody else asks. I've not decided if that's good yet, %1$s.
You're new. I've been wrong about new people before and I'm being careful.
Undecided. I'd rather say that honestly than say something warmer I don't yet mean.
You want it honest? There's a matter people haven't let go of, %1$s. I'm sorry to be the one.
Honestly — it's still being said, and I've not enjoyed knowing it and not telling you.
There's a matter. I'd rather you heard it kindly than overheard it unkindly.
Steady — and I don't say that lightly, %1$s, because I've been wrong about people before.
Hard to read, and I've been careful about deciding. I'd rather be slow than unfair.
You listen longer than you talk. That has mattered to me more than I've said.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.us.firs: ...You did, %1$s. Not anything you said. Just that you stayed, and nobody stays.

It wasn't a thing you said. I'd not remember a sentence. I remember you still being there.
...You don't remember. I've had that afternoon in my head for years, %1$s.
Right. Yes. It was only a small thing. To you.
...Sorry. I shouldn't have expected you to.
You want the story of how we met? Go on, then. I'll tell it my way, %1$s.
The story. I've told it to myself often enough; it'll be strange to say it out loud.
Right. Sit down. I've thought about that day more than I'd want to admit.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.us.futu: ...Work it out. Aye. That's better than one of us just giving in, %1$s, and I'd have given in.
Both of us. I'd braced for having to concede, and I'd have done it, and I'd have minded.
Neither surrenders. I didn't know that was on offer. Give me a moment with it.
That's fair. I'd rather that than a promise you'd resent, %1$s. I've had one of those.
Right. Nothing owed. It stings and it's the right kind of sting.
No promise. I'd have believed a promise and built on it. So — thank you.
...Never. That's a hard word, %1$s. Harder than I'd braced for.
Right. Yes. I'd rather you said it than let me keep hoping.
...I'm glad I asked. I'll be less glad about it tonight.
sensitive.dialogue.conversations.us.happ: ...You want to know, %1$s. Right. Small things — and you asking is one of them.
You asked. Nobody asks when things are fine, and I'd been saving these up alone.
Right. There's a list. I'd been frightened it would sound like ingratitude.
...I asked you a serious question, %1$s. It took me a while to get it out.
Right. Yes. I should have expected that and I hadn't.
...Sorry. I'll not put you on the spot again.
